hook_text: Seven clay faces, buried in a valley about one and a half thousand years ago. Who made them?
clip_script: Mashishing, Mpumalanga. In the museum, copies of the Lydenburg Heads stare out from the glass. They were made by some of the first farmers in southern Africa. These farmers grew sorghum and millet, kept cattle and goats, and lived in settled villages. Their ancestors came slowly from the north, family by family, over many generations. They spoke languages related to isiZulu and Sesotho. And they made iron tools in hot clay furnaces: the Iron Age.
visual_style: Whiteboard clay heads appearing behind glass, then a slow map of farming spreading south, then a glowing clay furnace.
mood: Mysterious and proud, like meeting very old ancestors.
pacing: Slow reveal of the heads, steady spread across the map, ending at the furnace fire.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out which crops your grandparents grew.
